subject: Private GPU runrate, egress split and provisioning currency for Aurelia Health
messages:
From: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@aureliahealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@aureliahealth.com
Date: 2027-08-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment sizing question — sustained runrate & egress split

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. We've pulled a short sample from production (attached) and the questions our infra team needs answered before procurement can commit: 

- We expect a sustained inference runrate of ~180 qps (inference requests per second) for 512-token average responses during business hours, with periodic bursts to ~850 qps for 2–5 minute windows up to 3x / day.
- Tail latency target: p95 < 200ms, p99 < 350ms (512-token payload).
- Multi-tenant plan: we'll be carving a private VPC pool but want predictable per-tenant currency so internal teams can budget.
- Network egress: roughly 40–50% of requests include payloads that cross to a partner service; we need guidance on egress bandwidth split and whether you recommend separate NICs / edge proxies.

Attached is a CSV with measured qps-by-hour and a preliminary cost target. Can you sketch a recommended starting cluster (GPU count/type, NICs, rack assumptions), and an initial SOW estimate? Also flag any warm-pool amortization we should plan for (cold-starts are expensive for our use case).

Appreciate a short runbook or options matrix we can take to procurement.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, Aurelia Health

Attachments:
- Aurelia_Measurements.csv (CSV, 46KB)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-21T12:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment sizing question — sustained runrate & egress split

Hi Sarah — thanks for the data and the clear asks. High-level summary up front, then a short options matrix below.

Quick answer (option we recommend):
- Sizing: Start with a 12x A100-80GB equivalent private pool (we'll map to the customer's chosen instance SKUs) giving ~220–260 sustained qps for 512-token avg with aggressive batching and KV-prefix caching.
- Burst headroom: Reserve a 3-node warm pool (autoscale-increment policy) to absorb 3x bursts to ~900 qps for up to 5 minutes without cold-start penalties.
- Network: Dual 100GbE NIC per rack, split traffic (inference/evidence egress) at the L4 edge with dedicated egress VPC path. Expect ~40Gbps egress during peak bursts given your 50% external payload rate.
- Warm-pool amortization: Recommend a steady-state warm pool target of 10% of committed capacity; amortize cost against runrate currency in the SOW.

Options matrix (capacity / risk / cost):
1) Conservative commit (recommended for regulated workloads): 12 GPUs reserved, 3 warm nodes, SLA-backed latency band, higher monthly commit but predictable cost.
2) Flexible commit (lower commit): 8 GPUs reserved + burstable pool on heavy traffic days, offload to secondary region if allowed. Lower monthly committed cost but higher engineering ops complexity to guarantee p99.
3) Minimal start (pilot): 4 GPUs, no warm pool; will meet daytime p95 but p99 will spike during bursts and cold-start amortization will be visible.

Deliverables we'll produce if you want: slot-level runbook (warm-pool choreography), egress split design (VPC peering vs. NAT gateway sizing), SOW with per-tenant currency (monthly base + usage credits for burst).

I'll loop in Karthik for network/burst math and Laura for SOW/contracting detail. If you can confirm whether cross-region fallback is allowed, we'll produce a short TCO estimate and an SOW draft.

Regards,
Hannah
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-22T08:31:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment sizing question — sustained runrate & egress split

Thanks — dug into the CSV Sarah sent. A few concrete numbers / assumptions so everyone has a shared model: 

Assumptions from our perf suite (512 tokens, Redwood optimized kernels, 80GB class):
- Single A100-80GB equiv GPU: ~20–24 sustained qps (with batching tuned to 8–12 concurrent inflight requests).
- Tail behavior: to hit p99 < 350ms under bursty arrival we need ~25% extra capacity above sustained qps (headroom + warm pool) because of queueing jitter.

Sizing math for Sarah's baseline (180 qps sustained):
- Base GPUs = ceil(180 / 22) = 9 GPUs.
- Add 25% headroom => 11–12 GPUs.
- Burst absorption to 850–900 qps for short windows: warm-pool of 3 extra nodes (3x GPUs, pre-warmed), or alternatively 4 GPUs if you prefer more concurrency per node.

Network:
- Estimate egress bandwidth at 50% payload external: 180 qps * 512 tokens * avg token payload 0.5KB => ~23MB/s sustained (approx 184Mbps). Bursts will multiply this; plan for 40–50Gbps headroom on the edge network for simultaneous parallel requests across the fleet.
- Recommend flow: Inference traffic on NIC-1 (internal), external egress on NIC-2 isolated with policy-based routing. Use eBPF filtering at the edge to prioritize small inference responses.

Operational notes:
- Warm-pool choreography: pre-warm KV cache on leader nodes, drain traffic via BGP weight adjustments on scale-in.
- Observability: instrument prefix-hit rates, queue-length histograms, and per-GPU token throughput. We'll include dashboards in the SOW.

I'll attach a quick spreadsheet with the math (exported) to the deal workspace. Laura, can you surface the recommended billing construct? Sarah, let us know if you have a target monthly commit (we can present a blended per-qps currency).

-Karthik
Principal Infra Performance Engineer
From: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@aureliahealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@aureliahealth.com
Date: 2027-08-23T10:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment sizing question — sustained runrate & egress split

Thanks — this is super helpful. Procurement is comfortable with a 12-GPU starting commit if we can get a clear SOW and a per-tenant runrate currency to present to finance. Two follow-ups: 

1) Can you call out the expected monthly base cost vs. variable burst credits (we expect to buy a small pool of burst credits to cover periodic peaks)?
2) Are there NIC / rack-level requirements from our data center team that we should put in the RFP? (they asked specifically about power draw per rack and 100GbE vs 200GbE options)

We'll sign off on the SOW draft if those pricing primitives are explicit. I'll also upload a redline to DocuSign once we receive the SOW.

Cheers,
Sarah

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-24T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment sizing question — sustained runrate & egress split

Sarah — looping with the SOW and pricing primitives you requested. Deliverables attached: Redwood_Provisioning_SOW_v1.pdf. High-level pricing construct below: 

- Monthly base (12-GPU committed pool): fixed fee covering reserved compute, warm-pool amortization (10% target), basic support and 30-day observability retention.
- Burst credits: pre-purchased tokens (or qps-minutes) bucket sold as credits applied when autoscale expands beyond committed GPUs. We price per qps-minute; example: 1000 qps-minutes = X USD.
- Egress surcharge: separate line item for cross-VPC egress above threshold; we include an estimated egress allowance (2TB/month) in the base.

DC/Rack asks for your RFP:
- Recommend 2x 100GbE uplinks per rack; 200GbE is optional but helpful for future growth.
- Per-rack power: plan ~12kW per rack at full load for 12x A100 class nodes (include a 15% buffer).
- Cooling and isolation: standard hot-aisle containment; we will provide heat maps.

I'll share the DocuSign link when we have the final redline. Hannah/Karthik — let's sync on the exact credit unit price and the egress allowance to land the SOW numbers.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachments:
